question: Do price jumps in decentralized prediction markets causally amplify media attention and induce self-fulfilling electoral expectations?
scope: 2024 US Presidential Election across 7 key battleground states (PA, MI, WI, AZ, GA, NV, NC) combining daily Polymarket CLOB settlement prices, 538 state polling averages, and public attention indices

searches.query: prediction market media coverage reflexivity election odds
rational inattention media gatekeeping price jumps bandwagon
identification through heteroskedasticity simultaneous equations Rigobon
Polymarket central limit order book election microstructure swing states

nearest_works.title: Prediction Markets
nearest_works.question: How accurately do prediction markets aggregate private information compared to traditional polling?
nearest_works.estimand_or_theorem: Information aggregation efficiency and forecast unbiasedness
nearest_works.method_or_proof: Descriptive time-series and correlation analysis of Iowa Electronic Markets
nearest_works.difference: Examines prediction markets as passive information aggregators; does not model or identify bi-directional media feedback or reflexivity.
nearest_works.prior_bottleneck: Evidence on forecast accuracy did not organize when market prices aggregate dispersed information or what contract design reveals.
nearest_works.innovation: Synthesizes theory and evidence across prediction settings and distinguishes probability, moment, and conditional contracts.
nearest_works.why_field_cares: Makes prediction markets an interpretable information-aggregation institution while explicitly retaining the correlation-versus-causation boundary.
nearest_works.validation: Compares market forecasts with outcomes and conventional benchmarks across multiple applications.
nearest_works.influence_or_reuse: Supplies the canonical passive-information benchmark that later market-design and microstructure studies test and refine.

nearest_works.title: Prediction Market Accuracy: Crowd Wisdom or Informed Minority?
nearest_works.question: Does prediction market price discovery stem from widespread crowd wisdom or concentrated informed capital?
nearest_works.estimand_or_theorem: Price response to large trades and market participant informativeness
nearest_works.method_or_proof: High-frequency Kyle lambda and order-flow Kyle decomposition
nearest_works.difference: Focuses strictly on internal market trading microstructure without examining downstream media reporting amplification or voter expectation feedback.
nearest_works.prior_bottleneck: Aggregate forecast accuracy could not reveal which participants actually create information or distinguish persistent skill from volume.
nearest_works.innovation: Uses the transaction universe and trader-level persistence to separate broad participation from price-discovering skilled accounts.
nearest_works.why_field_cares: Challenges both crowd-wisdom and insider-only accounts and changes which participation conditions sustain market accuracy.
nearest_works.validation: Tests whether classified traders predict future prices and outcomes, respond to public news, and correct cross-contract pricing violations.
nearest_works.influence_or_reuse: Creates participant-level measures that subsequent work can use to study liquidity, regulation, and information production.
nearest_works.frontier_case: Trader-level persistence and response to public news can distinguish broad crowd aggregation from information produced by a skilled minority.
nearest_works.selection_reason: It is a current RFS R&R and the closest evidence on who produces Polymarket price discovery, regardless of its still-low citation count.

nearest_works.title: The Anatomy of Polymarket: Evidence from the 2024 Presidential Election
nearest_works.question: How should on-chain Polymarket activity be measured, and how did market quality evolve during the 2024 election?
nearest_works.estimand_or_theorem: Exchange-equivalent volume, net inflow, disagreement, arbitrage deviations, and Kyle price impact
nearest_works.method_or_proof: Transaction-level blockchain accounting and descriptive market-microstructure analysis
nearest_works.difference: Builds the transaction and price-impact measurement foundation but does not identify a causal feedback effect from market prices to media attention.
nearest_works.prior_bottleneck: Raw on-chain flows mix exchange, mint, burn, and conversion operations, so naive volume and price-impact measures are not economically comparable.
nearest_works.innovation: Builds a transaction-level accounting decomposition that separates exchange-equivalent turnover, net inflow, and gross activity.
nearest_works.why_field_cares: Correct measurement changes conclusions about liquidity, price impact, disagreement, and alleged manipulation in tokenized markets.
nearest_works.validation: Applies the decomposition to the complete 2024 election ledger and checks consistent market-quality changes across arbitrage and Kyle-price-impact measures.
nearest_works.influence_or_reuse: Provides reusable measurement infrastructure for any on-chain prediction market before causal or microstructure estimation.
nearest_works.frontier_case: Correcting mint, burn, and conversion flows materially changes turnover and price-impact measurement before any causal analysis.
nearest_works.selection_reason: It is the nearest current measurement foundation and defines variables the proposed design would otherwise mismeasure.

contribution_statement: First study to formally establish theoretical micro-foundations of market-media reflexivity (Kyle-Sims-Callander dynamic Bayesian game) and to solve simultaneous bi-directional causality between prediction market odds and media attention using Rigobon (2003) structural heteroskedasticity identification on a 7-battleground-state daily panel.

limitations: Empirical sample is confined to the 2024 US Presidential Election across 7 swing states.
Direct voter ballot choices cannot be tracked at high frequency, requiring polling margins and public platform attention as empirical proxies.
Structural identification assumes constancy of structural transmission parameters across high- and low-volatility event regimes.
The legacy illustrative project lacks recorded researcher scope and contribution approvals.
